qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Controls 1.3 million hectares of productive Swedish forest land and renewable hydro assets, constituting irreplaceable physical infrastructure. However, downstream industrial outputs (paperboard, sawn timber, paper) are cyclical commodity price-takers. Group ROCE averages 6-9% through the cycle, falling short of the 12% threshold.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (Moat & Pricing). Exceptional owner of irreplaceable Swedish forestland and hydro power controlled by Lundberg, providing a generational store of real wealth. However, downstream wood, board, and paper products are cyclical price-takers, resulting in multi-cycle Group ROCE of 6-9%, below the 12% quality hurdle.
qualitative.evidence: Group ROCE was 9% in 2019, 6% in 2020, 9% in 2021, 13% at the 2022 cyclical peak, 8% in 2023, and 6% in 2024. Multi-cycle median ROCE (~8%) fails the 12% hurdle. Biological forest asset yields are inherently low (2-3%), and paperboard/timber products lack independent pricing power against global forest product cycles.
